distinguishing_features: Uses existing cathodic protection infrastructure to electrochemically stabilize the bearing surface via potential control, rather than chemical dosing
Leverages real-time pH and conductivity data to gate CP bias adjustments for localized passivation
Targets micro-galvanic corrosion under mechanical fretting by maintaining passive film integrity through electrochemical means
Eliminates need for consumable inhibitors or dosing hardware by using shipboard electrical systems
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to prevent corrosive wear in seawater-lubricated stern tube bearings without adding chemicals or hardware, using only existing shipboard systems and monitored parameters
parsed.viable_reason: The mechanism uses established electrochemical principles and existing CP systems with feasible current densities to maintain passivity under fretting conditions.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Prior art 2 relies on scheduled chemical dosing; using real-time water chemistry data to modulate electrochemical protection of a mechanically stressed bearing interface is not an obvious extension of inhibitor-based passivation.
